start.intro: Agentville turns the Claude Code sessions you run on this computer into characters in a pixel-art office. You keep working in the terminal as usual; Agentville shows what every session is doing. Four steps:

install.title: Install Claude Code
install.body: Claude Code is Anthropic's coding assistant for the terminal. Install it once with the official command for your system, then open a new terminal window.
install.gitWindows: On Windows, also install Git for Windows so Claude Code can run shell commands.
install.orButton: Or let Agentville install it for you →

login.title: Sign in
login.body: Run claude in a terminal. The first time, it opens your browser so you can sign in.
login.plans: Claude Code needs a Claude Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan, or an Anthropic Console account. The free plan doesn't include Claude Code.

connect.title: Connect Agentville
connect.body: In Settings → Monitoring setup, click “Set up automatically”. Agentville adds a small, reversible entry to Claude Code's settings so sessions report their activity. Sessions that were already open need to be restarted once.

work.title: Work as usual
work.body: Go to your project folder and start Claude Code. A character walks into the office and acts out what Claude is doing.
work.many: Every terminal session is its own character — open several to see a whole team.

office.intro: Each character is one Claude Code session, named after its project folder (rename and dress them with “Customize outfit”). The bubble above a character shows what it's doing right now:

legend.think: Working on your request (between tool calls)
legend.raise: Waiting for your approval in the terminal

office.screens: Monitors light up to match: code, terminal output, a question mark while waiting for you, a green check when done, a red cross on errors.
office.readOnly: Agentville only watches. Answer approval prompts, send messages or stop a session in the terminal where it runs.
office.inspector: Click a character to see its current tool, request, project folder, git branch and recent events. The activity log at the bottom keeps everything for 14 days.
office.controls: Drag to move around, pinch or +/− to zoom, F to follow the selected character. ✎ Edit office lets you rearrange furniture.
office.customize: Looks are saved per project folder, so the next session in the same project keeps its outfit.
office.demo: Demo mode plays a scripted story for exploring — it's clearly labelled and never mixed with your real sessions.

teams.subagents: When Claude delegates (for example to the Explore agent), a smaller character walks in, works next to its parent and leaves when done; a report flies back to the parent.
teams.teams: Claude Code's experimental agent teams let one session lead several teammates. Turn them on by adding this to ~/.claude/settings.json, then ask Claude to spawn teammates. Their shared task list appears in the sidebar, and finished tasks fly to the lead's desk.
teams.teamsNote: Agent teams are experimental and use more of your plan's usage.
teams.worktrees: To run several sessions on one repository without overwriting each other, give each its own worktree. Agentville groups sessions by repository and labels each with its branch.
teams.conflicts: If two sessions edit the same file in the same folder within a few minutes, Agentville warns you in the sidebar — a good moment to move one of them to a worktree.

noCharacter.q: I started claude but no character appears
noCharacter.a1: Open Settings → Monitoring setup and check that every item is ticked.
noCharacter.a2: Sessions that were open before you connected Agentville must be restarted once.
noCharacter.a3: Make sure you're in Live mode (top-left), not Demo.
noCharacter.a4: If the receiver shows an error, choose another port under Advanced and reconnect.

notFound.q: The terminal says “command not found: claude”
notFound.a: Close the terminal and open a new one so it picks up the new PATH. If it still fails, run the install command again or see the official troubleshooting guide.

permission.q: A character is raising its hand
permission.a: Claude is waiting for your approval. Switch to the terminal where that session runs and answer the prompt there.

cost.q: Does Agentville cost anything or use my tokens?
cost.a: No. Agentville only reads the activity Claude Code reports on your computer. It never calls Claude itself and needs no API key.

privacy.a: Nothing from Agentville. Claude Code sends activity to Agentville over 127.0.0.1 only. History stays on this computer for 14 days; you can clear it in Settings.

uninstall.a1: Settings → Monitoring setup → Advanced → Remove hooks (restores Claude Code's settings).
uninstall.a2: Quit Agentville and delete the app (Windows: Settings → Apps → Agentville → Uninstall).

closed.q: Claude Code shows “hook … failed: connect ECONNREFUSED”
closed.a: That appears when Agentville isn't running. It's harmless — Claude Code keeps working normally. Open Agentville to watch again, or remove the hooks (Settings → Monitoring setup → Advanced) if you don't use Agentville anymore.
